newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries easier in directionless Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries easier in directionless Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries eased in directionless Tokyo on Tuesday due to light profit-taking following overnight rallies.
Traders said falls in T-bond futures also dampened sentiment in the longer end of cash prices, but activity was mainly limited to position adjustments between dealers.

"The falls in the 10- and 30-year bonds were exaggerated by the market's thinness," a brokerage trader said. "We expect prices to move quietly during the Christmas holiday season." In New York, the market will have an abbreviated session. Business is expected to shut down at 1400 EST/1900 GMT on Tuesday.
The key 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond fell 4/32 to 98-24/32, yielding 6.60 percent, from the New York close on Monday.
March T-bond futures fell to 113-10/32 by late morning trade from the previous close of 113-14/32.

"I expect Treasuries to be range-bound until the end of the year as there are no major changes seen in underlying fundamentals and no more major economic indicators are scheduled for this year," the trader said.
Traders said the market's focus will be on the underlying sentiment of the U.S. economy which will be determined by trends during the Christmas shopping season.
